name: Red Herring
shortDef: Changing the subject to dodge the real question.
definition: Introducing a different topic that may sound related but doesn't bear on the question at hand, so attention drifts away and the original issue goes unanswered.
howToSpot: Restate the original question; does the reply actually answer it?
Notice when the topic shifts to something easier, nicer or more exciting
Ask whether the new point would change the answer to the old question
classicExample: Asked why rent went up 20%, the landlord talked about the beautiful new art in the lobby.
legitimateVersion: Raising a new point is fair when it bears on the question, like a mechanic noting other needed repairs, or when you answer the original question first and then add context.

contrast.fal_straw_man: A red herring changes the subject; a straw man stays on the subject but distorts the other side's position.
contrast.fal_tu_quoque: A red herring shifts to any unrelated issue; tu quoque shifts specifically to the critic's own behavior.
